question: How does Morgan Stanley convert workplace and stock-plan participants into wealth management clients?

claims.text: On the 4Q24 earnings call (published January 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said companion accounts were a focus when the E*TRADE and Morgan Stanley platforms were put together, and that integration is largely complete. She said the focus is now on channel migration: workplace assets that began in workplace and move into the advisor-led channel. She said that over the last five years or so, since 2020, $300 billion has come from workplace and moved into advisor-led.

On the 2Q25 earnings call (published July 2025), Ms. Yeshaya said new flows generated from workplace go into the advisor-led channel and are becoming fee-based flows. She said 70% of the flows that originate from workplace are net new assets to the firm, which she tied to the firm's investments in workplace.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (published January 2026), Chairman and CEO Ted Pick said the financial advisor workplace channel and the E*TRADE retail channel are each thriving. He said "The funnel is working." He cited net new assets of over $350 billion last year.

The January 2026 strategic update deck defines the measures behind the funnel. "Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE" are assets brought into advisor-led relationships where the initial account was workplace or self-directed, averaged across 2020 to 2024. "Core Client Relationships" combine Advisor-Led Households, Self-Directed Households and Workplace Participants, excluding overlap. Where relationships overlap across channels, they are counted in this order: Workplace, Advisor-Led, Self-Directed.

In the same deck, "Workplace Participants" are Stock Plan Participants, Institutional Consulting Participants, and Retirement and Financial Wellness Participants, excluding overlap. The latter two are participants of corporate clients serviced by Morgan Stanley at Work.

The 2025 10-K (published February 2026) describes the workplace channel as equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees. It reports 6.5 million participants and $534 billion of unvested assets at December 31, 2025, against 6.6 million and $475 billion at December 31, 2024. Individuals with accounts in multiple plans are counted in each plan.

The 1Q26 10-Q (published May 2026) shows stock plan unvested public assets of $475 billion and 6.6 million stock plan participants at March 31, 2026. It states that unvested stock plan assets are not included in client assets.

The 2Q26 10-Q (published August 2026) shows stock plan unvested public assets of $658 billion and 6.6 million participants at June 30, 2026. It describes Wealth Management as serving clients through three channels: Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace. Workplace services include stock plan administration.
The 3Q26 financial supplement (published October 2026) reports stock plan unvested public assets of $638 billion at September 30, 2026, against $658 billion at June 30, 2026.

In an October 2026 Morgan Stanley trade piece, Jeremy France, Head of Institutional Consulting Solutions, said helping people understand, engage with and use their plan is what elevates benefits into differentiators. The piece is about the retirement plan advisory market. It does not describe conversion into wealth management clients.

adjacent.text: Wealth Management net new assets were $232.4 billion in 3Q26, and fee-based asset flows were $80.5 billion.
adjacent.differs_because: These are segment-wide totals, not flows that originated in workplace or stock-plan accounts.

gaps.what: The dollar value of advisor-led flows from workplace and E*TRADE shown on the strategic update deck is not in the text provided, and neither is any participant-level conversion rate. The $300 billion since 2020 figure and the 70% net-new-assets share are management statements from calls.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley strategic update deck, slides 9 and 10 (January 2026), and quarterly earnings call transcripts

gaps.what: The evidence does not describe the operational mechanics of conversion, such as how advisors engage stock-plan participants or the offers and triggers used.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley at Work investor presentations or management commentary
